title: Needs some fixes - can’t track “not more than” habits
body:
I’ve been testing out a few habit apps at the moment. This one is nicely designed and I’d been using it for about a week. 

However, today I tried to add two goals which use the number tracking and should be successful if you do X not more than Y - for example, “Smoke not more than 10 cigarettes”. But when you go into track progress of these goals, they actually show as requiring you to do the task “at least” that many times to be successful - for example, smoke at least 10 cigarettes. This is definitely NOT what I want to track lol. 

I was going to provide feedback straight to the developer about this, but I couldn’t seem to find a “Contact us” option in the app. 

If you just need “yes/no” habits, or habits which require you to do “at least X” of something, then this app still may be useful for you.

title: Good function but serious problems
body:
I bought in-app premium upgrade of Habit Tracker (Habitbull) but I’ve encountered some problems. For one of the problems, I’ve emailed the developer’s gmail but got no reply. 

I have to use the app on different devices, but on my iPhone 8, it crashed twice. The problem is you can only see the starting picture but it will just quit and you have to delete and re-install the app to get it back to work. This problem didn’t happen again after two times. But I still would like the developer to check its full compatibility with new iPhones as the last update is 6mon ago. I still can bear this one. 

But now I have another problem. After sign out from my account, I would like to log in again to sync my data, but the app says my password is wrong. Because the password is stored in 1Password and I’m sure it was the original one. Even if I go to settings and tap “forgot password”, the system never sent email to reset the password. The funny thing is when I used the same email address and registered in the app with another password, it accepted the registration and then said I don’t have the premium function, which is not surprising because I can still use sync on my iPhone SE with the account registered with the same email. This reminds me of critical problems of the sync and server for this habit tracker app. 

I paid 7.99 dollars for this so I want the problem addressed ASAP, otherwise, I have to report problem to Apple App Store and refund. At least, please, THE developer, say something.

title: Tested most habit tracking life logging apps
body:
By far the best habit tracking and life logging application on the App Store!

I am a big believer in objectively tracking habits and using these personal 'big data' to better understand and gradually improving yourself. Over the past year, I have downloaded and tested most habit tracking and life-logging software on the App Store. Unfortunately, at this point in time most are simply inadequate lacking basic functionality such as the ability to go beyond yes/no answers by entering numbers, time spent. While the Boolean yes/no answer might work in some scenarios ("did I drink coffee today?"), often it takes more detail to understand habits in order to improve them over time ("how many cups of coffee did I drink this week?" "Am I still within my monthly limit of cups of coffee?"). A lot of good habits can simply not be tracked with yes and no as they involve time spent on something ("how many hours did I watch TV this week?"). Most apps don't make any discrimination between good habits that you would like to promote, and bad habits to be reduced. Other apps don't allow you to add a line of comment to data point entries to add qualitative comments to powerful numerical data. Another important area generally missing is data protection (these data are by there very nature personal and private) including backup of data and the ability to share data and statistics with your personal coach. Of course there are exceptions such as "Habit Tracker" app, but in this case the design is still quite basic, and it does not support the concept of successful streaks.

HabitBull is filling this gap. The app is very intuitive and well designed, yet comprehensive and powerful. I can easily define what "success" means even if this is as complex as a certain maximum number of coffees per week. The UI has streaks of successful days at its very core, which makes improving your habits very motivating. Success can also be redefined at any time without loosing historical data. The entry of data and qualitative comments is also intuitive and a minimum number of clicks away. HabitBull even has an optional social component to it with forums for those that look for peer support. At this point in time, I can highly recommend this app and believe that at the current pace of update releases there will be more great general features and improvements to come!

title: Very useful app but sync doesnt work / App très utile mais synchro ne marche pas
body:
Good app to not give up on long term goals that need regular habits !
But sync doesn’t work at all. I only use on the ipad where i downloaded it. Doesn’t work on iphone or another ipad. zero data synchronised, not even new habits ! Habits only were synced without data, after a reinstall. Therefore habitbull is a one device app only. And i have paid for pro. Unacceptable. Please fix or you will lose supporters for the next app that works.
March 2019 : still not fixed + app often crashes when opened.
May 2019 : still not syncing + often crashes. Nothing new from the developer for the last 11 months. It’s a robbery.

Bonne application pour suivre ses progrès et se motiver. Je me rends mieux compte de ce qui est possible avec une vue sur plusieurs semaines. Elle me permet de réévaluer mes objectifs de manière raisonnable pour ne pas craquer. Très bien pour les objectifs à long terme demandant de la régularité.
Mais la synchronisation ne marche pas. ce qui fait que je ne l’utilise que sur un appareil. Contraignant, pas moderne ! Pas acceptable pour une version pro payante. Serait vraiment géniale avec la synchronisation.
Mars 2019 : toujours aucune synchro, et de plus l’app se plante souvent à l’ouverture. Très agaçant.
Mai 2019 : toujours aucune synchro, ni manuelle ni automatique. Plantages récurrents. Dernière maj de l’app par le développeur il y a 11 mois. J’estime que les 19,99 euros sont largement volés !

title: Version 1.4.11 Finally seems to be working but  ...
body:
13 March 2020 Version 1.4.11

Despite raising yet another ticket number there was no response from the developers until a comment appeared on my previous review. The app finally seems to be working after nearly nine months of complaints. They have, at least, had the good grace to admit that I was right all along. The app stopped working at version 1.3.5 in June 2020 and despite numerous attempts, no other version has worked until now. I’ve finally managed to add back my data which the developers at one time said was corrupt. It wasn’t. I had the foresight to store it in another app. It took hours of work, as did writing constant reviews identifying the problems with each “fix”. The app now performs exactly as version 1.3.5 except for the addition of the annoying full-screen splash-ad every time it is started. The addition of the ad for the hugely overpriced subscription was the source of nine months of problems and annoyance to users. It is still annoying but at least it doesn’t seem to crash the app. I’ve upgraded my rating as promised but will hold off giving a five star rating until time has proving that it continues to work and the repetitive splash-ad is removed. To make it removal only on paying a massive subscription just makes people determined not to subscribe and to eventually charging to another cheaper, free or one-time purchase app. There are a lot to choose from that do exactly the same as Habit Bull. However, as the developers have clearly stated that I was right, I’m sure they are extremely grateful for my constant assistance and will show their gratitude....!

title: Big promise, big potential, no development and no replies...
body:
I actually paid the premium as I believe in the developer announcements about "this is only the beginning, we have big plans, we will be attentive to users requests" yet despite having a platform with great potential, there are some key areas where it lacks, which could be OK if there were signs of development - however last update (which was only a bug fix) was 9months ago, and I didn't get a reply to none of my email with questions and suggestions. 

Apologies for not writing all the many good things in it (enough reviews on that) but this is where it lacks:
* always displaying all habits, regardless of whether they are due today or not (creates unnecessary clutter)
* no daily/weekly score = you can't "feel" the improvement you are doing and not getting the encouragement to keep your score / average close to 100. 
* no reset of score of starting time of habit (in case you had a terrible start and now you want to begin in all over again. Only way is to delete it completely and recreate again). 
* you can only average a certain data per day (not per week/month. Like tracking "how many hours of sleep this week?" You can only enter data for daily, which is not always what we need (as in "ok last night was 6 but this one was 8 so I averaged 7, which is perhaps my weekly goal = 49hrs minimum")

It excel in other parts over the competitors, but a pity it's not being refined.

title: Dark mode errors
body:
Hi there, I’ve been enjoying this app for so long, but I would like to report on some errors that I’ve met with the latest update. First, it seems like you tried to integrate the Dark mode, which is a great idea. However, somehow only the lines with habit names get dark, and the rest of the screen is still white. Next, when the dark mode is on, and the lines with habit names are dark, the font used remains black. As a result, we get a black writing on the black background which means I can’t read the words.
Last, the advertisement. It doesn’t close when I press the X button and it asks me for confirmation on subscription instead of closing. It keeps doing the same thing every day. I hope you can fix this as well.
Thanks

title: Most sensitive customer data
body:
We all know what can happen when you save sensitive information to the cloud. I think that what you want to achieve in life is very sensitive data. It says a lot about you as a person.
Should you agree to HabitBull to save all your data in their cloud?
I rather not.
But when I choose not to save my data in their cloud I get a penalty.
When reinstalling my phone or the app I lose my payment information. I have to pay again.
Common HabitBull. Really?
Is this the way you steal the most sensitive data from your customers?

title: Good app, but just got aggressive
body:
I’ve been using HabitBull for a year now to help manage long projects (like reading every book I own, keep room clean, etc.). I’ve often wanted to upgrade but my finances are not at a place where I can justify in app purchases. 

So I resolved to use the free version until I pay off all my debt and get to a place where I’m comfortable spending. 

This last week, the app got really aggressive. I opened it to check off that I cleaned my room and it gave me a pop up asking me to buy it. Okay, I thought, can’t fault it for trying. I clicked on the x at the top, but instead of giving me the data screen, it acted like I’d tried to make a purchase. I cancelled it and it said purchase failed, but the screen stayed up, preventing me from entering my data for the day.  (Several hours later I managed to enter the data before I got the pop up again, with the same issue)

I’m hoping this is just a glitch, and will soon be fixed, not a punishment for longtime users who haven’t upgraded. 

Other positives about the app. I love that it lets you backtrack or go ahead. When one of my goals is to read a chapter a day, it’s nice to be able to make up days when I couldn’t get to it, or read ahead in anticipation of a family gathering/job/ class where I know I won’t have time.

body:

title: Great!! Has all the features for tracking
body: I’ve been using a very simple habit app for over a year, but realized I needed to change something because I’d do the habits for a while and then stop logging and checking progress. After listening and reading several habit related topics/podcasts I kept coming across the 80/20 idea. Basically, instead of being “good” or “bad”, as long as you shoot for compliance 80% of the time that might prevent you from dumping the whole effort after repeated “failures”. I looked through about 6 or 7 popular habit apps and this one seemed to have the best/easiest visual showing percentage adherence to goals based on various denominators ((day,week, month). I’m not far into my 80/20 experiment, but this app seems to be the easiest for assessing adherence in such a way. I will say that entering each habit was a bit of a pain, but it is completely customizable so that is great.

title: Goal tracking numbers flawed
body: I like the simplicity, but there is an error tracking goals with number requirements. When setting goals, you choose yes/no (you did it or did not do it) or number goals (you track a specific number of something). When you set a number goal, the default is “not more than” so you can put something like consume “not more than” 1500 calories. When the app actually creates the goal, it switches “not more than” to “at least”. So now the goal is only accomplished if you eat 1500 calories OR MORE. I have written to them at least 3 times and have only gotten an automated response. The problem may be corrected in the paid version, but I won’t risk spending money on the paid one if the free one works this poorly and I can’t get support for the problem.

title: Awesome - but a minor bug with a workaround
body:
I love this app.    It doesn’t manipulate me with games, challenges, or social motivators.  It doesn’t impose structure and time zones or a particular motivation theory.  

  I don’t need all those outside voices!  It does what I need: set simple goals that can be quantitative or qualitative; good or bad.  Then it makes tracking and reporting very easy.  

But there is a minor bug.  When you choose a numeric goal, you are given a choice for success.   It is either to perform above target (over 5 miles a day), exactly at target, or under target (less than 2 drinks a day).  
Unless you scroll through the options (roll up or down in the field) it may give you the wrong choice when you click save.

title: Great Functionality - try it & change your life
body:
HabitBull works flawlessly as described. You can get creative with how you create goals/habits if they overlap slightly and make the most of the 5 allowed in the free version. One example, I started with 3 individual goals each for one a snack during the day; this used most of my goal but after a week I reworked that to be one ‘numeric’ goal with three timed reminders through the day. Even with reworking this and making more space in the free app, I’m contemplating purchasing a month to see how I like the further functionality. 

For me, I’ve been down the road of calendar appointments but that causes real scheduling conflicts as well as the world of too many iPhone “Reminders” that don’t repeat exactly how I’d like. HabitBull has solved all of these functionality issues in a sleek and straight forward program!

I could never stick to flossing my teeth or working out until I downloaded this habit app. One of the most sufficient habit tracking apps for FREE that there is . title: Awesome app - developer doesn’t seem to be supporting it much anymore
body:
I’ve been using HabitBull for over a year now. I love how easy it is to customize my list, to check things off. I love the silly reminders and I love its simplicity, but it can do anything I want. It’s exactly what I want in a habit tracker app. 

I had a hard time finding it in the App Store. I’ve been using it on android and wanted to use it on my iPad. I had lost my login in password and tried multiple times to email reset it so I could login on the new device and never got an email (yes I checked spam etc.). On my iPad I also don’t see the motivation quotes, which was another feature I really loved. 

I think it’s overpriced for the premium version for the amount of support it receives. But I still use it because it tracks lots of habits better than anything else.

This app has been such a help at keeping me on track and so far has been one of the few things that has seemed to work in helping me cope with my problems as a result of my disorder. I can’t thank the creators of this app enough, this truly has been a godsend for me. Even after I build up habits I will more than likely keep using the app so I don’t relapse back into my old habits and forgetfulness.

body:
Downgrading my rating because the latest update with a note "Changes" fails to mention that the one time premium upgrade option has been removed and it's now a $19.99 subscription model with free version being ad supported. I wish there were more transparent about this change.

–-- Original Review 
I tried a bunch of streak and habit apps and found HabitBull the most easy to use and convenient design.

So why the 3 star rating? The look and feel needs to be updated to be more modern. And the initial startup/splash screen of the picture of the athlete should be removed. It's old school design and none of the modern apps follow anymore. I'd be happy to upgrade to premium if the additional themes were part of the premium package only or and add-on.

body:

I pinned it on right beside my Phone icon so I can access it easily.
It would be helpful if updates had more description about the changes, simply writing “Changes.” makes me want to reply back like “Oh, you don’t say?!” 😂, What changed? Even google writes a complete change log, it made me feel like I, as a user, am not worthy of an explanation (which I know is not the case).

P.S: I reduced my rating to 1 star. I can see what changed now, the pricing model! It was 4.99$ to unlock the premium features, now it’s 19$ a year! From a license model to a subscription model, and about  400% increase in price, and all you get while updating? “Changes”. This was a suicidal move. I’m done with this app.

title: Easy to use, customizable habits, motivational
body:
I started with a paper goal planner which was great for organizing the day but not do great for habit tracking to get to my goals.
Do I decided to try an app. I read reviews (many) and downloaded 5 apps. After adding sample habits to each and tracking for a few days, I settled on HabitBull. I liked that I could have a mix of habits that were weekly and daily. Some that I could only track M-F for work. Some that tracked negative habits like no more than 1 drink on a work night. And counting habits like 8 glasses of water a day. 
It’s easy to open the app and tick off that I drank my water with each glass. It’s also so satisfying (and motivating) to see I met all my habits for the day. Keeps my going!!
Love it!!!

title: Love it!
body:
I missed this app a lot when I switched over from Android, I’d check the App Store for it every so often until it finally appeared! I’ve been loving it ever since. I use it to keep track of all sorts of things. From personal habits to things I want to know whether I did or not and ask myself when the last time that thing happened was. It’s incredibly flexible and I love that I can go into the daily checklist and check off any of the things and easily see which ones are truly daily and due today and which ones I just need to update. I love being able to see the multiple views for daily, weekly, and monthly. My favorite is being able to check off something or if I’m wondering the last time I did something was, I can click it and it’ll take me to the month view so I can see at a glance. It’s extremely helpful in letting me see when the last I watered my plant was and more. I have reminders set for a few of them, and I love being able to confirm it on my Apple Watch when the alert pops up! 

The only things that would make me love this app even more are:

1. Apple Watch app with a complication so I can easily tap and check things off my daily list. 
2. A year view for each. This would be incredible to be able to see long-term trends without having to navigate between months.

Thank you again for all of your hard work! I looove this app so much! :)

This app hold me accountable for my habits, without making me feel bad about it. 
You set your own standards for the habits (every day, certain days a week, or a number of days in a week/month). I like this edit because it doesn't disqualify you if you don't do each habit every single day.

After using it for a few days I upgraded to premium to be able to have more than five habits. 

Two shortfalls, in my opinion: unable to start a habit earlier than today’s date (so if you exercised or flossed yesterday but didn’t enter the habit into HB until today, sorry, no two day streak), and if you have several habits, it is difficult to tell which ones you’ve actually checked off as done today without going through each one and looking at the calendar for that habit. title: Used to be great but terrible now
body: I used this app for years. It used to be great. But whatever the developers have been up to recently has made this app a frustrating experience to use. It crashes frequently, it only filled 2/3 of the screen on any device after iPhone X, it’s dark mode makes text unreadable, adding a habit is difficult because text doesn’t line up. Just sad how such a good app can be destroyed by unnecessary tinkering by developers. I’m deleting and looking for another habit tracker.
author: KratosGuy

title: Definitely recommend
body: Have been using this app for about a month now, and I’ve never been more consistent with my habits and other tasks. Love the look of the app. Premium is definitely worth it so you can track lots of habits, see the streaks grow, and be proud of the success YOU’RE creating. Only thing I don’t like is if you edit a habit it effects the past tracking. So if you had a habit that you did 3x per week, now you want to make it 4x per week, that new day added which previously would have been logged as yellow ‘don’t have to complete’ will now become red because of the edit, it thinks u were supposed to do the habit on that day. That then cuts ur streak to less than what it actually is. Maybe the developers can work on this, make any edits only future changing in the timeline of the habit. Otherwise I love it, and if you actually got to the bottom of this, get the app! It helps to get all ur tasks done without having to think and remember them all, all day!
